en: During a typhoon, storm surges can push seawater inland, so coastal residents must evacuate to higher ground before the winds arrive.
Soil containing animal waste can harbor tetanus bacteria, so you must wash cuts with clean water and soap immediately after playing outside.
Because surface runoff collects pollutants as it flows into rivers, you must always boil or filter this water before drinking it to prevent cholera.
Crushing certain minerals like asbestos releases microscopic fibers that damage lungs, so never break open unknown rocks without a proper respirator mask.
Looking directly at the Sun during a solar eclipse without certified eclipse glasses can cause permanent retinal damage due to intense ultraviolet radiation.
High humidity prevents sweat from evaporating, making the heat index feel hotter than the actual air temperature and increasing the risk of heatstroke.
The Moon's gravity causes higher spring tides during full moons, which can create stronger rip currents that pull swimmers away from the shore.
If you get lost at night in the Northern Hemisphere, you can find true north by locating the bright star Polaris in the Little Dipper.
If an earthquake causes the ocean water to suddenly recede from the shoreline, it is a natural warning that a destructive tsunami is approaching.
Lightning often strikes the tallest object in an area, so during a thunderstorm you should avoid standing near isolated trees or holding metal umbrellas.
Root crops like carrots absorb minerals directly from the soil, so you must thoroughly scrub and peel them to remove harmful dirt and parasites.
Concrete prevents rainwater from soaking into the soil during the water cycle, causing rapid flash floods in cities that can sweep away pedestrians.
